messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: state of branches?
parts:
Sorry again for all the chaos. Rearranging an existing
Git project is proving more difficult than anticipated.

One thing it would be good to know at this point is
the state of the various branches on our repository and
that you may have made on your own.

What I want to know is whether you have lots more locally
and for all of the above, what state are they in in terms of

a. readiness to be merged for next release

b. ease of recreation if the repository gets borked
(that is, how hard would it be to rebranch and
transfer the work over)

or if they should just be deleted.

On the repository, we have:

acid_tests
arg_refactor
circular
develop
diff_win_mac
feature/fix-chainable-delete
fix_test_models
fvar
graphical_diagnostics
identical_behavior
mcmc_writer

The three I know about are:

fvar: already merged, so should've been deleted

feature/fix-chainable-delete: this was my test example, which
is ready to merge and easy to recreate

develop: just added and reserved for future use

- Bob

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] state of branches?
parts:
None of those branches are anything I've touched or worked one.

I have a local branch (available on github) which I'm currently
getting into shape for a merge, ideally before the next release but
it's not the end of the world if it doesn't make it in. That branch
includes a lot of work to make GPs faster but also speeds up
multivariate normals a bit and implements a new distribution, the
matrix normal.

Cheers,
Marcus
